stories.headline: Saudi says it intercepted two drones launched by Houthis towards Riyadh
stories.deck: The Saudi civil defence had sent alerts overnight for Khamis Mushait ​and Abha ‌but not for the capital
stories.bodyText:
Yemen’s Saudi-led coalition said early on Saturday (September 26, 2026) it had intercepted two drones launched by the Iran-backed Houthis towards the Saudi capital Riyadh.
The coalition posted on X that it was monitoring missile threat and drones launched at the Kingdom without providing further details.
The Saudi civil defence had sent alerts overnight for Khamis Mushait and Abha but not for the capital.
The Houthis, who control the most populous parts of Yemen and much of the north, have been launching attacks against Saudi Arabia since declaring a naval blockade against Riyadh in July, with strikes targeting Saudi vessels in the Red Sea.
The attacks have targeted Saudi cities, energy infrastructure and shipping, adding to pressures on global oil supplies caused by the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran and putting at risk the main alternative Red Sea route for Gulf exports while traffic through the Strait of Hormuz remains largely blocked.

stories.headline: Trump rejects Iran's 7-day ceasefire offer, expects to resume bombing post midterms
stories.bodyText:
US President Donald Trump has rejected Iran's seven-day ceasefire proposal and told aides that he expects US bombing of Iran to resume after the November midterm elections, according to US officials cited by The Washington Post.
Tehran had offered to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and restart nuclear talks with the US as part of the proposed arrangement.
Under Iran's proposal, the United States would lift its naval blockade of Iranian ports, ease sanctions on Iranian oil exports and observe a ceasefire that includes Lebanon. In return, Iran would reopen the Strait of Hormuz and resume negotiations with Washington on its nuclear programme.
Meanwhile, Trump has said that Tehran is seeking a deal after the midterms that would dismantle its nuclear programme. However, according to The Washington Post, Trump privately remains skeptical that Iran would meet his demands and has told aides that renewed bombing is likely.
Trump is reluctant to resume major combat operations, partly because the United States wants to preserve dwindling munitions for other contingencies, the report said.
What was Iran's 7-day proposal?
Iranian foreign minister Abbas Araghchi said Tehran had offered Washington a seven-day framework under which the Strait of Hormuz could be reopened and nuclear negotiations resumed.
"If the necessary conditions are met, the strait can be reopened, a normal maritime passage restored within seven days. The choice now rests with the United States," he said.
“The seven-day timeline will start as soon as the United States accepts this plan,” Araghchi said.
Under the proposal, Washington would lift its naval blockade of Iranian ports, waive sanctions on Iranian oil sales and observe a ceasefire including Lebanon.
Araghchi said the initial measures would take four to five days, with the Strait of Hormuz reopening on the sixth day.
“And on day seven, the talks with the U.S. will be started for the final deal on mutually agreed subjects,” he said.
Araghchi said the measures Washington would need to take were already covered by the memorandum of understanding reached between Iran and the United States in June.
"The actions that the United States should should take are not new. They are all already in the MOU," he said.
The proposal was conveyed through Qatar, which has played a key role in mediation between Tehran and Washington.
US rejects lifting maritime blockade
The Trump administration has told Iran and regional mediators that the president has no intention of lifting the maritime blockade, officials familiar with the matter told Washington post.
Washington believes continued economic pressure could eventually force Tehran to accept an agreement with terms favourable to the United States and Arab states along the Persian Gulf.
A US official said Washington and Tehran were still negotiating through mediators, including on the nuclear issue.
An American-led effort to ensure oil tankers can continue sailing through the Strait of Hormuz despite Iranian threats has also reduced the urgency for an agreement, the official said.
The White House said US officials were engaged in positive and constructive conversations with mediators over the conflict and that the United States was facilitating oil exports through the Strait of Hormuz.
Trump says Iran must give up nuclear ambitions
Trump told world leaders at the United Nations General Assembly this week that domestic politics would not influence his approach to Iran.
“The Republican Party is running, and I’ll be helping them, but I am not running. I gave absolutely no credence and will not give credence through the election when it comes to Iran,” he said.
“The only thing that does is that Iran will never have a nuclear weapon.”
Trump has nevertheless told Republicans to act as though he himself is on the ballot during the midterm elections.
His current position indicates the conflict could shift back toward renewed hostilities, although US officials cautioned that Trump's views could change as the war continues and the midterm elections approach.
Trump has alternated between diplomacy, military action and economic pressure during the conflict. He has declared victory while also ordering strikes and tightening sanctions on Tehran.
He has at times threatened much broader military action to force movement in negotiations, while subsequently stepping back from his most expansive threats.
Why Hormuz matters
The Strait of Hormuz has emerged as one of Iran's main sources of leverage in its confrontation with Washington.
Before the war, about a fifth of the world's traded oil and gas passed through the strategic waterway, according to the report. Disruptions to shipping have affected energy markets and added pressure on the Trump administration ahead of the US midterms.
Iran's proposal linked the reopening of the waterway directly to the lifting of the US blockade, sanctions relief and a renewed diplomatic process over its nuclear programme.
The latest proposal resembles an interim arrangement discussed in June, although the new framework has a much shorter timeline.
The earlier arrangement envisaged a 60-day interim period and included sanctions relief on oil sales, access to frozen Iranian assets and recognition of a role for Tehran in administering the Strait of Hormuz in exchange for opening the waterway.
That arrangement subsequently collapsed after Iran resumed attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz.
Qatar pushes for renewed diplomacy
Qatar and other regional mediators have been working to revive indirect talks between Iran and the United States around the UN General Assembly.
Iranian officials had proposed a seven-day pause in fighting that could pave the way for an end to attacks on shipping in exchange for the United States lifting its blockade, according to people familiar with the discussions.
Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian also hosted Qatar's prime minister as diplomatic contacts intensified.
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Wednesday that “if there’s an opportunity to exchange ideas and messages, we will.”
Repeated failures to reach a lasting agreement have nevertheless left both sides deeply distrustful.
Hamidreza Azizi, senior Iran analyst at the International Crisis Group, said Tehran likely expected the latest proposal to be rejected.
“The Iranians already know that the chances of this not being accepted by Trump are much higher than the opposite,” he wrote on X.
“They want to show that they were ready for diplomacy and that it was the United States that, for the third time, decided to attack in the middle of a diplomatic track — something that people within (Iran’s) strategic community have been anticipating over the past few days,” he said.
Iran faces internal divisions over diplomacy
Iranian officials have sought to project unity, but the latest diplomatic initiative has exposed differences over how Tehran should respond to Washington.
Some hard-liners have called for continued military action and criticised President Masoud Pezeshkian and Araghchi for pursuing negotiations.
Firebrand lawmaker Ebrahim Rezaei wrote on X that meeting with “the aggressor enemy” demonstrated weakness.
Iran's Assembly of Experts, the body that appoints the supreme leader, said “there is no path other than resistance.”
Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Qalibaf, who previously served as a chief negotiator with the United States, acknowledged differences within Iran's leadership.
“There is a view that speaks of war but offers no prospect or mechanism for bringing it to a powerful conclusion,” he wrote on social media. “At the opposite end is a current that makes the error of underestimating national capabilities.”
He added: “The first error keeps the country in a state of permanent crisis, while the second hands national resources and dignity over to the enemy.”
Araghchi said more than 5,000 people had been killed in Iran during the nearly seven-month US-Israeli war.
Yemen conflict complicates Iran's proposal
Iran's proposal specifically refers to a ceasefire involving Lebanon, where Israel and Iran-backed Hezbollah have largely observed a ceasefire.
It remains unclear whether the proposal would also cover the renewed conflict involving Yemen's Iran-backed Houthi rebels and Saudi Arabia.
The Houthi attacks have added pressure on global energy markets and raised concerns about another strategic maritime chokepoint, the Bab el-Mandeb Strait at the southern end of the Red Sea.
Iran appears to view the Houthis' ability to threaten the Bab el-Mandeb as another potential source of leverage in negotiations with Washington.
Saudi Arabia has previously supported a return to negotiations and, according to a person familiar with the matter, had been open to an arrangement giving Iran a temporary role in managing the Strait of Hormuz.
However, Saudi calculations changed after the Houthis seized Yemen's strategic Red Sea coast from pro-government forces and a vital Saudi pipeline came under attack.
An earlier planned meeting of Gulf leaders in Oman to discuss an emerging Oman-Iran agreement on Hormuz was also cancelled after Saudi Arabia sought amendments to the proposed arrangement.

briefs.headline: Congress leads protests demanding CEC’s resignation, arrest
briefs.deck: Modi, Shah using Kumar to overcome public opposition through “artificial manipulation”, says Venugopal; civil society groups hold agitations in Delhi and other States; police use water cannons to stop protesters
briefs.bodyText:
The Congress on Friday (September 25, 2026) led nationwide protests demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar, accusing him of compromising the integrity of India’s electoral process, with the party’s general secretary (organisation), K.C. Venugopal, seeking Mr. Kumar’s resignation and arrest for alleged electoral malpractice. Civil society groups and other organisations held parallel protests in Delhi and several States.
Congress workers took to the streets across the country, with protests in several places being stopped by the police. Water cannons were used against demonstrators in Patna, Lucknow, and Punjab, while protesters were detained in Assam, Jammu, Odisha, Manipur and other States. In Manipur’s capital, Imphal, the police fired a few tear-gas shells to disperse the protesters.
In Kerala’s Malappuram, Mr. Venugopal said the nationwide protests would continue until the CEC stepped down. Targeting Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Home Minister Amit Shah, the Congress leader alleged that they were using Mr. Kumar to overcome public opposition to the government through “artificial manipulation”.
“Resigning alone is not enough; he must be arrested. What he did is a criminal offence; he must be arrested,” Mr. Venugopal said, adding that all decisions taken by Mr. Kumar, including those relating to the special intensive revision, should be revoked.
In a post on X, he urged every Indian to mount “unbelievable pressure on the regime and its puppet for the daylight robbery of our vote and fix accountability”.
The party’s communication chief, Jairam Ramesh, said citizens and Congress workers hit the streets demanding accountability over the capture of their fundamental right to vote and the “Chief Election Commissioner’s diabolical mischief”. “The frightened Modi Govt has cracked down on protesters and detained Congress leaders and workers, young citizens and students, and civil society activists – in so many places across the country,” he wrote on X.
Congress leader Pawan Khera told a press conference: “We want to say to Gyanesh Kumar: it’s done bro. Heed Rahul Gandhi’s advice – resign and turn approver.”
The Congress accused the Election Commission of an “unprecedented attack” on voter equality, alleging that a specific ‘Mark VIP’ feature had been created in the BLO application.
Amid mounting pressure from the Opposition, CEC Kumar cancelled two scheduled meetings in Uttar Pradesh. Poll body sources said these were not linked to the protests and were routine decisions.
At Jantar Mantar in New Delhi, the campaign drew participation from civil society activists and organisations. The All India Students’ Association (AISA), along with civil society members, organised a protest demanding the arrest of Mr. Kumar. CPI(ML) Liberation general secretary Dipankar Bhattacharya, AISA president Neha Bora, activist Yogendra Yadav, lawyer Prashant Bhushan, RJD MP Manoj Jha, activists Anjali Bhardwaj and Nandita Narain were among those who participated. Several protesters, including Mr. Bhattacharya and Mr. Yadav, were detained by the Delhi Police.
Delhi Congress chief Devender Yadav, who had organised a march from the Delhi Congress office to Nirvachan Sadan, the Election Commission’s headquarters, was also detained by the police. Another protest was called by the Students’ Federation of India outside Nirvachan Sadan. The Indian Youth Congress separately staged a protest in Delhi in which demonstrators wore masks bearing Mr. Kumar’s face and displayed their hands in chains.
New Delhi Deputy Commissioner of Police Sachin Sharma said protesters were detained as no permission had been sought or granted to hold the protest at these venues. Mr. Sharma said that 50-60 protesters were detained from Jantar Mantar, around 10 from the SFI protest, and around 25 from the Congress protest.
The All India Democratic Women’s Association took out a rally from Kolkata’s Esplanade to the office of the Chief Electoral Officer (CEO) and later submitted a memorandum to the CEO demanding the CEC’s resignation.
The Congress has framed the protests around its “vote chori” campaign, alleging that the electoral-roll revision process could exclude legitimate voters. The protests followed Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi’s press conference on Thursday on the issue, after a news report that two of the three Election Commissioners, Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi, had repeatedly objected over a period of 10 months to decisions on the electoral rolls, saying that some of the decisions were taken without their knowledge.
In several States, party workers burnt effigies of the CEC, raised slogans demanding his arrest and called for an independent review of the electoral rolls.
In Patna, the Bihar Congress marched towards the Election Commission office but was stopped by the police using water cannons. Similar protests were reported in Lucknow, where Congress workers led by State president Ajay Rai clashed with the police after being stopped. In Assam, State Congress president Gaurav Gogoi and other leaders were detained when they attempted to march towards the Chief Electoral Officer’s office.
In Jammu, Congress MP and AICC general secretary Syed Naseer Hussain led the protest, with several senior party leaders, including former Ministers and former legislators, participating in the demonstration.
The Congress also alleged that the Narendra Modi government was trying to deny Gen Z voting rights by attempting to “snatch [them] away through underhand means”, recalling former Prime Minister Rajiv Gandhi’s decision to lower the voting age from 21 to 18.
“One PM gave Gen Z the vote, the other is determined to snatch it away through underhand means,” Mr. Ramesh said in another post on X.
Published - September 25, 2026 10:56 pm IST

briefs.headline: Attacks on commercial shipping in Gulf, Red Sea simply indefensible: Jaishankar as India and Liberia announce ‘group of friends’
briefs.deck: A terrorist country is asking me that question, the External Affairs Minister said in strong response to Pakistani journalist at the UN
briefs.bodyText:
External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar on Friday (September 25, 2026) listed recent incidents of attacks against seafarers and ships, saying “regrettably” these are no longer exceptional occurrences. His remarks came as India and Liberia announced establishing a “group of friends” on the safety and security of shipping and seafarers, on the sidelines of the 81st UN General Assembly.
The initiative was launched at the ministerial-level meeting of the group of ‘Friends on Safety and Security of Shipping and Seafarers’. “India, as a major source of seafarers, and Liberia, as the largest shipping registry, have come together to highlight the safety and security of shipping and seafarers,” Mr. Jaishankar said at the meeting.
“In the last few months, commercial shipping and marinas have been subjected to repeated attacks in the Gulf, the Red Sea, and its vicinity….These actions that disrupt maritime commerce and cost innocent lives are simply indefensible,” he added.
Amid ongoing global conflicts, merchant shipping and seafarers are facing increased risks in various regions, including the Strait of Hormuz, Gulf of Oman, Red Sea, Gulf of Aden, Bab-el-Mandeb, Black Sea, and Somalia.
A significant number of Indian seafarers serve onboard both Indian-flagged and foreign-flagged vessels operating in or transiting through these regions, exposing them to associated maritime security risks
A terrorist country is asking me that question: Jaishankar to Pakistani journalist
Mr. Jaishankar also sharply responded to a Pakistani journalist who asked him a question related to terrorism.
"A terrorist country is asking me that question. Come on,” he said in a strong response to the question by the Pakistani journalist at the UN
After India and Liberia’s remarks at the UN headquarters, the Pakistani journalist stood up and shouted a question to Mr. Jaishankar, “When will your government stop sponsoring terrorism in Pakistan?”
India’s Permanent Representative to the UN, Harish Parvathaneni, told the Pakistani journalist: “You have heard your reply. You have heard your response, loud and clear.”
On Thursday (September 24, 2026), an Indian journalist had asked Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, as he entered the UN building, "When will you stop harbouring terrorists?"

briefs.headline: IMD issues heavy rain alert for September 26–27 in Uttarakhand; CM Dhami directs officials to maintain vigilance
briefs.deck: The Chief Minister appealed to residents and tourists to exercise extreme caution and urged people to travel only if essential and after checking the latest weather and road conditions.
briefs.bodyText:
After the India Meteorological Department issued 'red' and 'orange' rain alerts for several Uttarakhand districts for September 26 and 27, Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami directed officials on Friday (September 25, 2026) to remain on high alert.
The Chief Minister appealed to residents and tourists to exercise extreme caution and urged people to travel only if essential and after checking the latest weather and road conditions.
Red alert issued
According to the weather forecast, a 'red' alert for heavy rain has been issued for five districts on Saturday (September 26, 2026): Bageshwar, Pithoragarh, Champawat, Nainital, and Udham Singh Nagar. An 'orange' alert has been issued for five other districts -- Dehradun, Pauri, Rudraprayag, Chamoli, and Almora -- while a 'yellow' alert is in place for the remaining three districts: Haridwar, Uttarkashi, and Tehri.
For Sunday (September 27), a 'red' alert has been issued for four districts -- Dehradun, Tehri, Pauri, and Haridwar; an 'orange' alert for four others -- Uttarkashi, Chamoli, Nainital, and Rudraprayag; and a 'yellow' alert for the remaining five districts -- Bageshwar, Almora, Champawat, Udham Singh Nagar, and Pithoragarh.
The meteorological department has forecast heavy to very heavy rainfall in many places and extremely heavy rainfall in some areas during this period. Consequently, mountainous regions face a risk of landslides and road blockages, along with rising water levels in rivers and streams. Waterlogging could occur in the plains.
Mr. Dhami urged the public to follow the guidelines issued by the local administration. He advised people to avoid venturing near rivers, streams, seasonal watercourses, and waterlogged areas during heavy rainfall, and warned against entering fast-flowing waters.
He urged people to exercise extra caution on vulnerable roads and in landslide-prone areas within the mountainous regions. The Chief Minister also appealed to parents not to allow their children to go near rivers, streams, or other hazardous locations.
He directed officials and concerned departments to remain on high alert and continuously monitor sensitive areas -- specifically river and stream water levels, landslide-prone zones, mountain routes, the Char Dham Yatra routes, and major tourist destinations.
The Chief Minister emphasised the need to ensure all necessary preparations are in place so relief and rescue operations can begin immediately in the event of any potential disaster. He instructed that relief and rescue teams, along with essential equipment, JCBs, and other machinery, be kept ready at strategic locations.

briefs.headline: Quote of the day by Sylvester Stallone
briefs.deck: Sylvester Stallone shares his reflections on the dual nature of success and failure, emphasizing the importance of choosing one's battles wisely. He advocates for focusing on what is genuinely important, drawing from his own challenging journey in Hollywood, especially before achieving fame with 'Rocky.' The iconic character, Rocky Balboa, epitomizes resilience and the idea of personal…
briefs.bodyText:
Failure is something almost everyone experiences, but learning what is worth fighting for can change the way we look at it. Sylvester Stallone once spoke about this while reflecting on life, success and the legacy of his most famous character, Rocky Balboa. His words offer a simple idea: we may not win every battle, but the ones that truly matter deserve our effort.
Today’s quote of the day by Sylvester Stallone reads: “I’m a big believer that, in life, we can’t succeed in everything. Most times, we lose. But the few times we do win, we have to make sure they were the important battles.”
What does the quote by Sylvester Stallone mean?
The actor expressed these thoughts in a 2006 interview with Total Film when explaining why he wanted Rocky to be remembered for the inspiration the character gave people. Stallone’s words seem to suggest that success does not have to be measured by winning every argument, competition or challenge. Some fights aren't worth wearing ourselves out over.
Disappointments are in life. Plans go awry, opportunities are lost, and sometimes even our best efforts do not give us the result we hoped for. Stallone’s argument is that failure is not necessarily a failure in life. The key thing is knowing where to put our energy.
The second part of his thought is especially important. If there are only a few moments when everything falls into place, those moments should involve things that genuinely matter to us. That could mean a career goal, a relationship, family, personal growth or a dream that we have refused to give up on.
Why does his message still matter today?
Modern life can make success look like a competition that never ends. One person is announcing a new job, another is celebrating an award, while someone else is sharing a new relationship, business achievement or personal milestone.
Also, it is important to realise that not every setback needs to stay on our mind, and not every argument is worth spending our energy on. Sometimes, knowing what to leave behind can be just as important as knowing what to fight for. Sometimes, moving forward means knowing what to let go of and where to put your energy. Sometimes walking away from something is also a form of strength.
His words also encourage people to think about priorities. Instead of trying to win everywhere, it may be more meaningful to protect the relationships, ambitions and values that matter most.
Sylvester Stallone’s early life
Born on July 6, 1946, in New York City, Stallone did not enter Hollywood with an easy path to success. A medical complication at the time of his birth left Stallone with partial paralysis affecting some facial muscles. That condition became part of Stallone's distinctive screen presence, from the way he spoke to the expressions he made while acting.
His journey in Hollywood was anything but smooth. Long before audiences knew him as an action star, Stallone took whatever small acting work he could find. Money was often tight, and finding steady work was not easy.
With acting opportunities limited, he started putting more time into writing. It was a decision that eventually opened a completely different door for him. The story he wrote would go on to change the course of his career.
Sylvester Stallone’s rise to fame
Everything changed for Stallone when 'Rocky' arrived in 1976. He had written the screenplay and also played the lead, and the film quickly turned into a major success. It also earned him Academy Award nominations for his performance as well as his writing.
Ultimately, “Rocky Balboa” was far more than a character in a boxing movie. His story touched people's hearts because it's about getting back up when things go wrong and continuing to believe in yourself. Stallone returned to the role over the years, with 'Rocky Balboa' bringing him back to the character in 2006.

stories.headline: Nandini milk price may go up by Rs 5 per litre; CM’s call today
stories.deck: In Karnataka, district milk cooperative unions have urged the government to boost the price of Nandini milk, suggesting an increase of Rs 5 per litre due to escalating costs and challenging drought conditions. Initially, they requested a rise of Rs 8 to Rs 10 but later scaled back their demand. The local dairy farmers are also grappling with competition from private companies offering better…
stories.bodyText:
BENGALURU: All 16 district milk cooperative unions of Karnataka Milk Federation Friday urged the state govt to increase Nandini milk price by Rs 5 a litre on the back of severe drought, rising input costs and widening losses.
Chief minister 
DK Shivakumar
 is expected to decide on the proposal on Saturday. If approved, the price revision will be the fourth in three years. The unions had sought an increase of Rs 8 to Rs 10 per litre, along with a similar hike in incentive paid to dairy farmers. Later, they pared it to Rs 5.
Drought, rising costs
A litre of blue-packet milk (toned) is currently priced at Rs 46, green (special) at Rs 50 and orange pack at Rs 52
The govt is looking to strike a balance between improving farmers’ returns and shielding consumers from a sharp price shock.
Bangalore Milk Union president DK Suresh said milk cooperatives are under financial pressure in the past 6-7 months. “KMF has maintained low prices in public interest. With private dairies aggressively procuring milk at higher rates, Karnataka’s milk cooperatives are facing pressure to remain competitive,” he added.
Sources in KMF said Karnataka’s milk producers remain among the lower-paid dairy farmers in South India. While farmers in Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh and Maharashtra receive more than ₹41 per litre, Karnataka producers receive around ₹35.
KMF, which handles 60 lakh litres of milk a day, is said to be losing ₹60 lakh a day amid the widening gap between procurement costs and consumer prices.

stories.deck: 4 Bengaluru Election Areas Account For 90% Of 2L Notices Yet To Be Sent Out
stories.bodyText:
Bengaluru/Mysuru: Karnataka
 has delivered 41.6 lakh of the 43.8 lakh notices generated under the special intensive revision (SIR) of electoral rolls over logical discrepancies, and the remaining notices are yet to be sent out as of Friday, according to the chief electoral officer’s (CEO) office.
Bengaluru Urban, BBMP South, Central and North entities account for nearly 90% of the 2.1 lakh notices which are yet to be issued. Since hearings must be completed by Oct 12, these notices must reach voters not later than Oct 5 so that they get a week’s time to keep documents in order and prepare defence for re-inclusion of names in the rolls.
The notices seek clarification from voters, whose entries showed logical anomalies or could not be mapped to the 2002 electoral roll and enumeration forms, including mismatch in names, age or parent details.
The CEO’s office said 28.8 lakh hearings had been completed, accounting for 69.2% of the delivered notices. The remaining 12.8 lakh hearings are to be completed by Oct 12, while Oct 22 is the deadline for disposal of notices, claims and objections.
The corrected names will be reflected in the final electoral roll scheduled to be published on Oct 27.
Eleven districts — Kolar, Hassan, Chitradurga, Kodagu, Shivamogga, Bagalkot, Ballari, Vijayanagar, Ramanagaram, Chamarajanagar and Davangere — have completed notice delivery. 
Voters receiving notices have been asked to appear before the AERO or ERO with one of 11 indicative documents, including passport, birth certificate or SSLC marks card, to establish their identity.
Seven districts have less than 100 notices pending, with only one in Koppal. Five districts have 100-500 notices pending and four districts have 500-850 notices in the to-be-sent folder.
Mysuru deputy commissioner Lakshmikanth Reddy said they have a month to complete the process. Names of 250 dead voters and those having multiple voter entries had surfaced in the draft roll in Mysuru. These entries are being removed through Form 7.
The district-wise figures show considerable variation in the pace of hearings. The chief minister’s home district Ramanagara has completed 91.91% of hearings after generating and delivering all 19,696 notices. Chikkamagaluru has completed 87% of hearings after delivering 99.45% of its 91,610 notices, while Davangere has completed about 85% and Shivamogga 83% of hearings.

BK Hariprasad
 accusing BJP MLA Abhay Patil of demanding deletion of 2,500 minority voters from his constituency, Belagavi South.
Of the 61,130 Form 7 applications received across Karnataka, no voter has sought deletion of another person’s name through this provision. “The number of forms received for objection for proposed inclusion is nil,” the CEO’s office said.
A senior official told 
TOI that all such applications were from voters themselves or their families, asking to remove their own entries.
For the record, MLA Patil has rejected the allegation, saying he had sought verification — not deletion — of the voters’ antecedents.

stories.headline: BWSSB expands jurisdiction to cover entire Bengaluru Urban district
stories.deck: With the fresh notification, the jurisdiction now extends across the entire district, taking in five taluks in full, including North, East, South, Yelahanka, and Anekal and villages within them
stories.bodyText:
The Urban Development Department (UDD) on Thursday notified an expansion of the operational reach of the Bengaluru Water Supply and Sewerage Board (BWSSB), extending its jurisdiction to cover the whole of Bengaluru Urban District.
Till now, the BWSSB’s reach was limited to the core city area, comprising the erstwhile seven City Municipal Councils (CMCs), one Town Municipal Council (TMC), and 110 villages, spanning roughly 800 sq. km.
With the fresh notification, the jurisdiction now extends across the entire district, taking in five taluks in full, including North, East, South, Yelahanka, and Anekal and villages within them.
The BWSSB will now be responsible for the planning, implementation, operation, and maintenance of drinking water supply, underground drainage systems, and safe sewage disposal through treatment plants across the newly added areas.
Combined masterplan
A combined master plan will be prepared for the entire Bengaluru Urban district outside the Greater Bengaluru Authority (GBA) limits to ensure assured drinking water and sewage infrastructure, Greater Bengaluru Development Minister Krishna Byre Gowda said on Friday.
The Minister said that the BWSSB has been directed to assess drinking water requirements for the next five and 10 years and beyond. The plan will cover water storage, treatment plants, and distribution networks.
A similar blueprint will be prepared for underground sewage networks and sewage treatment plants, Mr. Gowda said, adding that the implementation will be taken up in phases in line with urban expansion.
The directions were issued at a meeting involving the BWSSB, Bengaluru Metropolitan Region Development Authority (BMRDA), and Minor Irrigation Department.
Groundwater levels
The Minister said that the exploitation of groundwater has skyrocketed beyond sustainable levels, and an external intervention is required to restore groundwater levels. For this purpose, the government had also directed the Minor Irrigation Department to prepare plans to use treated wastewater from Bengaluru to fill lakes around the GBA limits, he noted.
The government said the agencies had been instructed to prepare detailed plans for consideration, with the objective of addressing infrastructure needs ahead of urban expansion.
Mr. Gowda said that the move comes as urbanisation has crossed GBA limits, with rapid growth taking place in municipalities and gram panchayats surrounding the city.

stories.headline: Karnataka government to double refreshment allowance for pourakarmikas
stories.deck: Chief Minister D.K Shivakumar says that a Cabinet sub-committee will be constituted to address the demands of civic workers, including issues related to their boards, welfare and welfare funds
stories.bodyText:
Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar on Friday announced that the State government would soon issue an order increasing the refreshment allowance for pourakarmikas from ₹35 to ₹70.
Speaking at the Pourakarmikas’ Day programme in Palace Grounds, Mr. Shivakumar said that a Cabinet sub-committee would be constituted to address the demands of civic workers, including issues related to their boards, welfare and welfare funds.

The government plans to construct Karnataka Public Schools (KPS) in urban areas for the children of pourakarmikas, he said. “Our aim is for your children to study, become leaders and create new employment opportunities. We want your children to become IAS and KAS officers,” he added.
Mr. Shivakumar said that the government had decided to provide ₹7.5 lakh for the construction of houses for civic workers. He also announced that a pourakarmika bhavan would be built, and the work would begin within two months.
He said as many as 12,609 porakarmikas had been regularised since the Congress government came to power in 2023, while 6,000 workers had been appointed in local bodies.

briefs.headline: Teachers’ SIR work could hit exam results: Karnataka minister
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru:
 Teachers staying away from campuses due to SIR have affected academic activities in schools and could adversely affect students’ results in future, school education and literacy minister Madhu Bangarappa said Friday.
“Deployment of teachers from govt and aided schools for SIR is severely disrupting children’s education. As this task drags on, classroom teaching is suffering,” he told the media at his official residence in the city.
The minister said the state govt had repeatedly written to 
Election Commission
 asking it to exempt teachers. “Although we wrote to Election Commission stating that children’s education is being severely hampered, there has been no response. The EC is acting without any sense of humanity,” he said.
Complaints are received from schoolchildren and their parents over the problems teachers face due to SIR duties. There have been reports of schools being left without teachers and children being sent home after the midday meal, he said and emphasised that such a situation cannot be allowed to continue.
“Mid-term examinations are currently underway in the state and preparatory exams are scheduled for the near future. 
The absence of teachers from schools raises worries about how students will effectively face these exams,” he said.
“Teachers are exhausted by their SIR duties. The prolonged nature of this task has created a situation where academic activities in schools are not proceeding properly,” he said.
TOI
 wrote about the draft Karnataka Protection of Teachers from Non-Educational Deployment Bill in these columns on Sept 24. One of the highlights of the proposed law is the creation of a non-teacher public duty roll. For this, govt will maintain district-wise rolls of non-teaching personnel from all departments, statutory boards, corporations, public sector undertakings (PSUs), retired public servants, and trained volunteers. These resources must be utilised in full before any teacher can be considered for deployment.
“We intend to place it before the cabinet and introduce the bill during a future legislature session,” said Madhu.

briefs.headline: Two terror suspects arrested in Karnataka
briefs.bodyText:
A four-month-old Telegram message app trail has put two youngsters in the police net in Chikkaballapura, with investigators probing allegations of terror-related discussions, recruitment and plans to raise funds for extremist activities. The accused are Shabbir, a resident of Bapujinagar in Chikkaballapura, and 
Salman
, who is reportedly from North India.
Acting on intelligence inputs, police first arrested Shabbir from his residence and subsequently took Salman into custody. Cops are examining the Telegram group, its administrator and alleged network of individuals linked to it.
According to preliminary findings, Shabbir, a PU dropout, had joined Telegram around four months ago and was allegedly involved in discussions concerning terror activities. Police suspect the group discussed plans to target pro-Hindu leaders and kidnap wealthy individuals for ransom, with the money allegedly intended to finance terror activities. Chikkaballapura SP Padmini Sahoo confirmed the arrests.

briefs.headline: No civic response? Citizens roll up sleeves and fix potholes, roads in Bengaluru
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru: When petitions to civic authorities don’t yield action for months, citizens pick up a sandbag, bitumen and trowels, start fixing potholes and level off roads.
Citizen activism has gone from online clicks and signing petitions to real-world civil work. Meet software engineer Uday S and his wife Ashwini P, from Sir M Visvesvaraya Layout in west Bengaluru. After three months of complaints and calls, the couple bought road-repair material and started filling potholes. They have spent Rs 10,000 so far.
Their initiative is part of Bengalureans’ growing frustration with civic authorities. Uday had been raising complaints about roads in Visvesvaraya Layout with Bengaluru West City Corporation for months.
The BDA layout was handed over to GBA in January. Though BDA informed the corporation about the transfer, residents said the potholes continued to remain a problem. Uday said the response was initially prompt when the commissioner was monitoring complaints through phone-in programmes. After April, getting through to officials became increasingly difficult. “I’ve contacted every official and engineer possible, many of whom have stopped receiving our calls,” he said.
Citizen fixes a pothole in Bengaluru
Uday travels from Kengeri to Whitefield three days a week. He has seen commuters fall and suffer injuries on Bengaluru’s battered roads. He is also a victim. With little action on the ground, Uday and Ashwini decided to take matters into their own hands and filled potholes in the night when traffic volume is thin.
Getting material was a challenge. Dealers were reluctant to sell bitumen to individuals, with some asking for road contract documents or insisting on bulk purchases. Eventually, one dealer agreed to supply them with 10 bags of cold-mix asphalt, each weighing 10 kg and costing Rs 750. Including delivery, the couple’s bill came to nearly Rs 10,000.
Now, Uday has started repairing roads in Rajajinagar, where his parents live.
Patience wears thin, startup founder fixes Koramangala road
A startup founder in Koramangala got a broken footpath fixed after waiting for two months. Siddharth Dialani said he had raised complaints through GBA WhatsApp helpline, 1533 and by email to GBA chief commissioner, but saw no action on the ground. He spent Rs 2,700 to fix a stretch on Koramangala 3rd Block 8th Main. And his act went viral.
Not just roads, entire system is broken: Activist
Bengaluru Navanirmana Party founder Srikanth Narasimhan said civic apathy was a direct result of the absence of elected local representatives. He said the system itself — not just roads — is broken. “The city is suffering from a disease called ‘centralisation’.” Narasimhan has completed 25 reality-check walks under BNP’s ‘Freedom from Bad Roads’ initiative, covering multiple places in south and east Bengaluru. He has been receiving requests from across the city.

briefs.headline: Karnataka CM doubles pourakarmika snack allowance to Rs 70
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru:
 Pourakarmikas requesting that their daily snack allowance be raised from Rs 35 to Rs 50 got an unexpected boost Friday, with chief minister 
DK Shivakumar
 announcing that it would instead be doubled to Rs 70.
The announcement came at the state-level Pourakarmika Day celebrations at Palace Grounds, where thousands of civic workers had gathered. Worker representatives had sought an increase to Rs 50, but Shivakumar went a step further. “There was a demand to increase it; I want to increase it to Rs 70,” he told the workers, adding: “If you are healthy and strong, our streets, city and public health will also remain strong.”
The CM had another surprise in store. In a symbolic gesture of solidarity, he and several ministers donned pourakarmika uniforms and shared lunch with the civic workers.
Calling pourakarmikas “nation builders” and “ambassadors of cleanliness”, Shivakumar said their work was vital to public health and urged them to perform their duties with dignity and self-respect.
He also assured the workers that the remaining 6,800 civic workers awaiting regularisation would be made permanent at the earliest. 
Around 28,000 pourakarmikas have already been regularised, he said, adding that govt will also set up a cabinet sub-committee comprising officials from the finance, social welfare and urban development departments to examine the workers’ long-pending demands.
Other announcements included a dedicated Poura Bhavan for civic workers and residential schools for their children on the lines of 
Karnataka
 Public Schools.
The CM, however, flagged complaints about some workers not discharging their duties properly, saying the actions of a few should not affect the reputation of the larger workforce. “About 60% are genuinely doing their work every day, but the actions of the remaining few affect the reputation of the entire community,” he said.

briefs.headline: Karnataka may cut drug agents, stockists from hospital supply chain
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru:
 Rattled by spurious drugs flooding the market, govt is contemplating a new system for procurement of medicines by hospitals that could require them to source drugs directly from manufacturers, cutting out intermediaries such as carrying and forwarding (C&F) agents and stockists, health minister UT Khader told 
TOI.
The proposal comes amid an ongoing investigation into the Bidadi spurious drug racket. FDA has so far cancelled licences of 16 retail and wholesale firms and suspended eight others, including a 
Pfizer
 C&F depot in Nelamangala, as part of the probe.
“There is an established chain aimed at making drug distribution easier and creating more employment opportunities. But having so many stops between the company and the final user might create unforeseen obstacles and make it difficult to fix accountability. This is why we are trying to streamline these channels, similar to what is being done in Uttar Pradesh. This might even help in reducing cost of drugs as a lot of commission will be cut,” Khader explained.
The minister’s remarks came after a meeting with representatives of Pfizer and senior health department officials. He said govt is examining the possibility of restructuring the procurement chain after identifying a similar pattern in Belagavi.
According to Khader, a pharmacy at KLE Medical College and Hospital in Belagavi had procured 15,300 vials from a Pfizer C&F at a discounted price, claiming the medicines were needed for the hospital. An acknowledgement was subsequently issued by the hospital for receipt of the stock. However, the hospital required only 140 vials, while the remaining was allegedly sold in the market by the pharmacist at a higher price, Khader said.
Investigators suspect some of the spurious medicines linked to Krupa Health Care, the wholesale drug centre allegedly operated by a key accused in the Bidadi case, may have been mixed with this consignment and entered the market. These allegations form part of the ongoing investigation and have not been independently established.
Khader said the episode raised questions about the regulatory requirements for C&F agents. “We need to ensure these people have at least some technical knowledge and expertise. We will design some fixed rules,” he said.
The minister said further action on the proposed changes will be taken after a national conclave of Food and Drug Administration officials scheduled to be held in Bengaluru in Oct.
What UP did
The proposed 
Karnataka
 changes are being considered against the backdrop of Uttar Pradesh’s recent order on institutional drug supplies. The UP drug regulator tightened traceability requirements for medicines supplied to hospitals and other institutions at special discounts. Such medicines must be billed to the intended institution, delivered to the destination and marked ‘institutional supply’ on the packaging.
Safety is our priority: Pfizer
Pfizer issued a statement on the ongoing investigation into counterfeit medicines in Karnataka. “Patient safety and product quality are our highest priority. We have been working with the authorities over the past month when the matter of counterfeit medicines was brought to our attention. Since then, we have taken several actions to support the investigation, including removing from the market Pfizer batches (where batch numbers were copied by counterfeit) to avoid confusion, supporting to differentiate between original and counterfeit products, and providing technical and other relevant information related to the affected batches.”

briefs.headline: Ministry of Minority Affairs signs MoUs with prominent institutions
briefs.deck: The MoUs have been signed with the Centre for Urbanisation, Buildings & Environment (CUBE), IIT Madras; Foundation for Science Innovation and Development (FSID), IISc Bengaluru; Indian Institute of Management Bangalore (IIM- B); and IIM-B Innovations (NSRCEL)
briefs.bodyText:
The Ministry of Minority Affairs, Government of India, entered into several Memoranda of Understanding (MoUs) with prominent academic, research and innovation institutions at IISc, Bengaluru.
The MoUs have been signed with Centre for Urbanisation, Buildings & Environment (CUBE), IIT Madras; Foundation for Science Innovation and Development (FSID), IISc Bengaluru; Indian Institute of Management Bangalore (IIM-B); and IIM-B Innovations (NSRCEL).
“These partnerships will enable the Ministry to access specialised technical and academic expertise, strengthen evidence-based decision-making, improve monitoring and assessment mechanisms, support innovation and entrepreneurship, and create stronger institutional pathways for capacity building and enterprise development,” said a statement from the Ministry.
Third-party monitoring
An agreement was signed with IIM-B for independent third-party monitoring of training under Pradhan Mantri Virasat Ka Samvardhan (PM VIKAS) scheme across the South zone.
Under this partnership, IIM-B will conduct field-level inspections and concurrent monitoring, assessing training delivery, infrastructure, beneficiary and trainer participation, attendance, certification and placement outcomes through on-ground verification and stakeholder consultations.
The evidence-based insights generated through the partnership are expected to help the Ministry strengthen implementation quality, identify and address gaps, improve monitoring mechanisms and enhance outcomes under PM VIKAS.
Strengthening entrepreneurship
The two tripartite MoUs signed by the Ministry of Minority Affairs, National Minorities Development & Finance Corporation (NMDFC), with FSID, promoted by IISc, and NSRCEL, the entrepreneurship and incubation centre of IIM-B, will establish a framework of cooperation to strengthen the startup and innovation ecosystem and promote economic growth of minority communities.
The collaboration with FSID focuses on startup ecosystem development, innovation promotion and technology commercialisation, along with data governance, digital transformation and public interest technology.
The MoU with NSRCEL focuses on strengthening the startup ecosystem, along with skilling and capacity building, innovation and entrepreneurship promotion, research studies, policy support and evidence-based decision-making.
Assessment of PMJVK
The Ministry signed an MoU with CUBE, IIT Madras, for independent third-party quality (technical and social) assessment of infrastructure projects under the Pradhan Mantri Jan Vikas Karyakram (PMJVK) scheme. The assessment will cover selected and ongoing PMJVK projects across the sectors of education, health, skill development, women and child development. It will focus on key parameters, including infrastructure quality, functionality, accessibility, utilisation, maintenance and sustainability.
The partnership is expected to provide the Ministry with independent, evidence-based assessments and actionable recommendations, enabling better asset management, identification of implementation gaps and more informed planning for future PMJVK projects.
“The focus of the government is ‘EEE’ — to enable employment through entrepreneurship,” said Srivatsa Krishna, Secretary, Ministry of Minority Affairs, at the event.

briefs.headline: Bengaluru police issues guidelines to curb harassment, extortion by transgender persons
briefs.deck: The move follows complaints about incidents at traffic signals, markets, bus, and railway stations, residential areas and function or ceremony venues.
briefs.bodyText:
The Bengaluru City Police have issued guidelines to regulate complaints involving transgender persons allegedly harassing members of the public, obstructing traffic, aggressively soliciting money and engaging in other unlawful activities at public places.
The move follows complaints about incidents at traffic signals, markets, bus, and railway stations, residential areas and function or ceremony venues.
According to the guidelines, police have been instructed to verify the facts and circumstances of every complaint involving aggressive solicitation of money or alms, obstruction of public or vehicular traffic, threats, abusive behaviour, assault, or harassment, and take appropriate legal action in accordance with law.
Police stations have also been directed to identify locations within their jurisdictions from where repeated complaints are being received and arrange increased patrolling in such areas.
The police have been instructed to conduct regular meetings with members of the transgender community and create awareness against involvement in unlawful activities.
At the same time, the public will be informed about the immediate steps they can take when faced with harassment or violations of law.
The guidelines stress that while maintaining public order and ensuring smooth movement of traffic, the legal rights, dignity, and respect of transgender persons must be protected.
Police personnel have been specifically directed not to use derogatory, insulting or abusive language against transgender persons and to use respectful and non-discriminatory language while taking action against violations.
The Commissioner of Police has instructed all officers and personnel of Bengaluru City Police to strictly comply with the guidelines.
The public has also been advised not to panic during such incidents and to immediately contact the 112 emergency helpline, provide details of the incident and lodge a complaint at the nearest police station.
Rakshitha Mallikarjuna, a transwoman and social activist, acknowledged that there had been instances of transgender persons forcing members of the public to give money or behaving rudely. However, she argued that such a move could lead to excessive action against a community that is already marginalised, as it could create the impression that all transgender persons behave in the same way.
“We demand respect. Whatever money comes should be accepted without demanding or forcing. But why is seeking alms or any action by a transgender person being specifically notified against, while men, women, and even children are not warned against in a similar manner? Such measures may give the police the power to act against the community,” Rakshitha added.

briefs.headline: SIR in Karnataka: The right to vote, on trial
briefs.deck: Weeks into the hearing process of the Special Intensive Revision, many are still trying to find their notices and understand why they had been called, while others who had completed their hearings are seeking clarity from the Additional Electoral Registration Officers. The burden has been particularly visible among marginalised sections, especially women and daily-wage workers.
briefs.bodyText:
“It would have been better if our family’s names had been deleted. Filling another form would have been easier than getting documents to prove that we are citizens here in Chikka Banasawadi, where we have been living since 1961,” said Lakshmi Devi, whose family survives on daily-wage construction work and waste picking. Four of the six members of her family have received notices for “unmapped with last SIR”.
Her father, she said, had voted in at least 30 elections from the same place. But the family has no documents other than Aadhaar and ration card; they have no land title because the area is an unnotified slum, and nobody in the family can read or write.
Getting the documents in the Election Commission’s indicative list would cost at least ₹600-₹700 per document, she said. Most of the documents in the list require people to pay to apply for them or to obtain the supporting paperwork. For instance, a passport requires an application fee, while applying for a caste or permanent resident certificate involves affidavits and other paid documentation.
Not far from here, at Siddartha Nursery and Primary School in Lingarajapuram and Merry Mount Nursery, Primary and High School, both hearing centres in the Sarvagnanagar Assembly constituency, hundreds of people waiting with files, photocopies of documents and, in most cases, only Aadhaar cards, had similar doubts.
Across hearing venues, questions such as “Is it finally done?”, “Will we be called again?” and “Does this mean our name will be there in the final rolls?” could be heard. Weeks into the hearing process, many are still trying to find their notices and understand why they had been called, while others who had completed their hearings were seeking clarity from the Additional Electoral Registration Officers (AEROs).
While several said the hearing itself took only a few minutes, the process leading up to it had taken a toll: from finding their names in the list and receving the notice, spending money on documents, missing work and travelling to the hearing centre, only to leave without knowing whether they would be called again or if they would remain on the rolls.
With the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) now in its last phase in Karnataka, 43.81 lakh people across the State have been issued notices. Of these, 24.05 lakh are in Bengaluru. These are people who had already made it to the draft electoral rolls and are now being asked to appear before officials and produce documents to establish their eligibility to remain on it.
The notices have been issued broadly to two groups - those for whom a link to the 2002 electoral rolls could not be established, and those flagged for “logical discrepancies”. The latter includes nine categories, covering differences in names or parents’ names, implausible age gaps between an elector and their parents or grandparents, among other reasons.
The pattern of notice generation has raised concerns. People said notices appeared to have been generated in bulk for the same discrepancy, including in cases where they believed they had filled out their enumeration forms correctly, but still “entire families“ were flagged. Such cases were flagged in Bapuji Nagar, Peenya, and reported by many apartment residents where residents said the entire block got notices.
Some said BLOs had told them that filling all details in Kannada avoided a mismatch during transliteration, lowering the chances of discrepancy flagged by the software, while others said they had been asked to wait for a notice despite having submitted all the required details.
This was evident when the officials in Bengaluru Urban initially acknowledged that at least three such cases had come to its notice in Byatarayanapura, where people who had submitted their forms correctly had nevertheless received notices for “no mapping”. The flagged names were still required to appear for a hearing at the ADEO (additional district election officer) level.
This also stood in contrast to the prompt and unconditional relief extended in cases involving “VIP voters”, who were assured that such errors would not require them to go through the same hassle and that their name would be directly added to the final rolls “noting their contributions”.
However, for lakhs of common citizens, even finding out who had been issued a notice became another task.
The Chief Electoral Officer’s office put the notice list online on September 6, after public pressure, but there was no communication to tell people where or how to check it. Many said they came to know of the list only when links were circulated on WhatsApp groups. In some apartment complexes, residents printed the lists themselves so others could check their names. Many assumed they had nothing to worry about because their BLO had not told them anything, until they received a call asking them to collect a notice or appear at the nearby polling station with documents many did not have.
The burden has been particularly visible among marginalised sections, especially women and daily-wage workers. In Byatarayanapura, of the 21 domestic workers The Hindu interacted with, 16 had been marked as “unmapped with last SIR”.
Gangamma, one of the domestic workers, pointed to her enumeration form and said she had given her EPIC card to the Booth Level Agent (BLA), who filled in the details. Yet, she and her son were marked as having no mapping. Her son, who works as an auto driver, has a matriculation certificate. Gangamma has nothing beyond an Aadhaar card and ration card. “If I am not eligible, will my son be eligible? Will we not be getting ration from next month?” she asked.
For many women, the difficulty has been producing documents in their own names. Most of the women appearing for hearings said they had not studied beyond class 8, had no land records or birth certificates and, in some cases, could not obtain caste certificates because doing so required a transfer certificate they did not have. Several were asking whether their husband’s, father’s, or brother’s documents would be accepted in their place.
For senior citizens too, the documentary requirements could stretch back generations. Some said they had been asked to produce documents relating to their parents and, in some cases, even their grandparents. “Asking a 78-year-old person for their grandparents’ documents is forcing a person to give up on the vote by will,” said a retired government officer who attended a hearing in C.V. Raman Nagar.
Despite repeated assurances that every eligible voter will be “included,” citizens pointed out that an exercise of this scale has failed to account for the realities of migration, informal housing, daily-wage work, and limited access to government records. With limited safeguards and time to respond, several voters said they felt they were being treated as “suspects,” while those marked as ASDDO (Absent, Shifted, Duplicate, Dead and Others) were deleted even before verification.
At the same time, the publication of the ASDDO data without sufficient communication, similar to the notice list, created another layer of confusion. Many electors understood being listed as “shifted” or “absent/untraceable” in the ASDDO list as equivalent to receiving notice.
Manjunath, an auto driver, said: “My wife filled my enumeration form, but then I learnt that my name had been flagged only after a neighbour sent me a link.” Worried that he could lose his vote, he paid ₹1,250 for a permanent residence certificate, which is yet to be processed, and went to his brother’s school to get a transfer certificate, believing these were the documents he needed. He later found that his name was not on the official notice list and that the link through which he had checked his name was not from the Chief Electoral Officer’s office.
The link shared with Manjunath was among several third-party websites that began offering searches using EPIC numbers and data from enumeration forms. The personal electoral data of 5.54 crore electors was searchable outside the CEO’s official platform, allowing people to find out whether they had been flagged for a logical discrepancy even before the CEO officially announced that such discrepancies would be acted upon. Despite this apparent breach of electors’ privacy, the CEO’s office took no action against these websites, beyond advising electors to check their details only on the official website.
While those on the draft roll were navigating notices and hearings, those whose names were deleted at the draft stage faced a different hurdle of getting back on the roll. The claims and objections window, which was running alongside the hearings, ended on September 23. New voters and those marked as absent or shifted were directed to apply through Form-6.
But the number of Form-6 applications has been far short of the scale of deletions. Over 6.96 lakh applications had been received as on September 20, against 80.62 lakh electors deleted as shifted or absent, suggesting that not even one in 10 deleted names applied for inclusion, though the figures also include new voters.
“Migration” and “urbanisation” were among the key reasons cited for undertaking the SIR, besides identifying suspected foreign nationals. Yet, in Bengaluru, it is precisely the movement of people from one place to another that has emerged as the dominant reason for deletion. The overwhelming majority of deletions have been attributed to electors being marked as “shifted” or “absent”; in most constituencies, the two categories together account for at least 90% of deletions. In some cases, members of the same family were marked “shifted” or “absent”, while others in the same family received enumeration forms.
Moreover, there is also no appeal against being marked as ASDDO. Once a person is put in the ASDDO category and therefore deleted, the decision is treated as final, and the only remedy offered to the person is to fill a Form-6 and apply as a “new voter.”
The scale of the deletions is particularly stark in Bengaluru when compared to districts where the overall deletion stands at 13%, against 45% deletion reported in Bengaluru. Statewide, at 36 polling stations, deletions were between 70% and 90%, according to the CEO’s data, while in two polling stations — in Sarvagnanagar Assembly constituency in B.B.M.P. North district and Kodagu district — more than 90% of the names deleted. More than 20 of these 36 polling stations are concentrated in Bengaluru Urban alone.
Against these mismatches and mass deletions, civil society groups have been pressing for the deletions in the draft roll to be taken to the gram-sabha level and read out, so that names can be checked at the community level and verified against the ASDDO data.
There is a precedent for such a community-level verification. In 2003, then Chief Election Commissioner J.M. Lyngdoh had ordered decentralised social audits of electoral rolls through gram sabhas and ward sabhas in five States going to the polls. In Rajasthan alone, the exercise led to more than seven lakh corrections, with community-level verification identifying duplicate, deceased, and non-resident electors and adding eligible voters.
Even the Election Commission’s 2023 manual for “summary revision“ had specifically directed Electoral Registration Officers to have BLOs read out the draft rolls of each part at gram sabha or ward committee meetings in their polling-station areas. The SIR 2025 manual, however, does not even mention any such reading-out of the draft rolls.
Meanwhile, problems reported during enumeration, including people not receiving enumeration forms and difficulties with the Kannada-only process, continued into the notice phase. Several people complained that notices were available only in Kannada, despite the CEO’s categorical assurance that notices in Bengaluru would be available in both English and Kannada, and in Kannada and one other language based on regional need.
Moreover, while the CEO’s office said on September 18 that 79.79% of notices had been “delivered”, people said BLOs had not come to their homes but instead called them to hearing venues and asked them to sign stating that the notice had been delivered.
BLOs, however, said they were not given even breathing space and had been working under extreme circumstances since May.
“I rented a vehicle when I was told to deliver notices. But later, officials said the priority should be to scan and upload notices at the hearing venue itself, and upload photographs following the hearing,” a BLO said. The BLOs, especially from the Education Department, had also sought exemption from other duties, pointing out that students had not studied through the year because there were no teachers.
On questions such as whether filling forms in Kannada could have led to a discrepancy, and how they had been trained for the notice phase, several BLOs said they were “clueless” through much was kept in the dark about their role in the notice phase until the enumeration phase ended. “Less than a week before the BLO work was extended for the notice phase, we were informed about it. How can there be any training?” a BLO argued.
She said BLOs themselves faced frequent glitches on ECINet, including transliteration errors, and had no scope to verify or correct the information before notices were generated in bulk. Several BLOs said they tried to help people wherever possible. “Even in many cases of hearing, to complete the process, copies of Aadhaar and ration cards have been accepted because the majority of people flagged do not have any documents. But even we don’t know what will happen during the final rolls as these are not indicative documents,” she said.
Chief Electoral Officer V. Anbu Kumar was not available for a comment.

stories.headline: Govt weighs mandatory blending of imported coal at power plants, sources say
stories.deck: Under the plan being discussed ‌by officials of the Power Ministry, thermal power plants would have to blend ‌up ⁠to 5% imported coal with domestic coal
stories.bodyText:
India is considering telling power plants to blend imported coal with domestic supplies for the first time since 2024, three government sources said, to ease a supply crunch that has pushed monthly spot power prices to their highest since 2022.
Higher global coal demand and rising freight costs are set to make imports costlier, as Indonesian prices are up about a fifth since May while Russian prices are 14% higher and South African rates are up 19%, traders say.
Under the plan being discussed by officials of the Power Ministry, thermal power plants would have to blend up to 5% imported coal with domestic coal, said the sources, who are directly aware of the matter.
The plan represents a sharp reversal in New Delhi’s drive to boost domestic coal production and curb imports, which helped prune overseas supplies over the past two years.
Most of India’s coal-fired power plants rely primarily on domestic coal, but can blend up to 15% imported coal. Indian coal imports are already at a 15-month high.
The government’s previous coal-blending directives ran from December 2021 to March 2024.
Falling coal stocks at power plants
But coal inventories at power plants have fallen nearly twice as fast as a year before as September electricity demand held at levels seen during India’s broiling summer, in contrast to previous years’ pattern of receding.
Stocks fell nearly 49% in the three months to September, compared to a decline of 26% in the year-ago period.
The rapid depletion of coal stocks is prompting New Delhi to consider mandating imports, two of the sources said.
The discussion is at an early stage and aims to save domestic coal for use next summer, one of the sources said.
All three sources spoke on condition of anonymity as they were not authorised to speak to the media.
The Union Ministry of Power and the Ministry of Coal did not respond to a request for comment.
Nearly 40% of India’s coal-fired power plants now hold less than three days of coal stocks, leaving utilities with little cushion as consumption outpaces fresh supplies.
Power sector grapples with weather woes
While warm temperatures have boosted power demand, a weak monsoon has hit hydropower generation.
At the same time, heavy rains in some coal-producing pockets of eastern India have disrupted mining, while constrained rail capacity has slowed the movement of coal to power plants.
Renewable power generation rose about 21% year-on-year but fell short of round-the-clock energy needs, ratings agency Crisil said.
The supply crunch has pushed spot power prices to an average of ₹7.71 per unit so far in September, the highest monthly level since 2022, data showed, putting further financial pressure on already debt-laden state power distributors.

stories.headline: JSW One Platforms files draft papers for ₹3,054 crore IPO
stories.deck: The proposed IPO comprises a fresh issue of equity shares worth up to ₹1,300 crore and an Offer for Sale of shares worth up to ₹1,754.01 crore
stories.bodyText:
JSW One Platforms Ltd, a technology-enabled B2B platform serving the manufacturing and construction sectors, has filed draft papers with the market regulator SEBI to raise up to ₹3,054 crore through an initial public offering (IPO).
The proposed IPO comprises a fresh issue of equity shares worth up to ₹1,300 crore and an Offer for Sale (OFS) of shares worth up to ₹1,754.01 crore, according to the draft red herring prospectus (DRHP) filed late on Thursday (September 24, 2026) night.
The OFS will comprise shares sold by JSW Steel Ltd, JSW Cement Ltd and Mitsui & Co Ltd.
The company plans to use the net proceeds from the fresh issue to invest ₹125 crore in JSW One Distribution Ltd towards marketing and brand-building activities, ₹500 crore in JSW One Finance Ltd to augment its capital base and up to ₹350 crore for technology and platform development.
The remaining proceeds will be used for general corporate purposes.
JSW One Platforms operates an integrated digital platform that connects MSMEs with sellers of manufacturing and construction materials. Its offerings include commerce, embedded financing, logistics, processing and customisation, and private brands.
As of June 30, 2026, the platform had 95,611 registered customers, 1,713 sellers and 165 cumulative brands, with a network spanning 6,963 serviceable pin codes.
The company is supported by 81 logistics partners, 12 contract service centres and 9 contract manufacturers.
Its revenue from operations rose 44.93% to ₹5,743.39 crore in fiscal 2026 from ₹3,962.81 crore in the previous fiscal.
Gross merchandise value (GMV) increased to ₹18,596.91 crore in fiscal 2026 from ₹12,564.84 crore in fiscal 2025.
For the three months ended June 30, 2026, the company reported revenue from operations of ₹1,642.45 crore, while profit after tax stood at ₹14.21 crore. Its GMV was ₹5,949.73 crore.
According to the 1Lattice Industry Report, India's B2B trade is estimated at around $2 trillion. The addressable market for manufacturing products was estimated at ₹8.84 lakh crore in fiscal 2026, while the market for construction products was around ₹11.30 lakh crore.
Digital penetration of B2B commerce across India's manufacturing and construction sectors stood at around 3% in fiscal 2026E, indicating significant scope for further digitisation, the report said.
JM Financial, Kotak Mahindra Capital Company, ICICI Securities, SBI Capital Markets and PL Capital Markets are the book-running lead managers for the issue, while KFin Technologies is the registrar for the offer.
